events.text: The Presidential Leadership Council launches a large-scale military operation against Houthis in Yemen, with the aim to capture all Houthi-controlled territories.
A Yemeni government offensive pushes the Houthis from the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
Brazil's benchmark Índice Bovespa index rises nearly 9% to almost 210,000 points after the first round of the presidential election, surpassing 200,000 points for the first time.

Russian president Vladimir Putin approves the restructuring of UniCredit Bank Russia and the subsequent sale of most of the business to a United Arab Emirates-based private investor, while UniCredit retains its payments operations.

The United States Air Force withdraws all of its B-1 Lancer strategic bombers from RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, England. The U.S. Department of Defense confirms the bombers have returned to bases in the United States.
A Nigerian Air Force ATR 42-500 aircraft carrying 32 people crashes in Ondo State, Nigeria.
The death toll increases to over 30 people, with dozens still missing, of the two ships that collided yesterday on the Congo River near Lukolela, Democratic Republic of the Congo.

events.topic: International Criminal Court investigation in Afghanistan
events.text: The International Criminal Court unseals arrest warrants for Taliban education minister Habibullah Agha and higher education minister Neda Mohammad Nadeem, accusing them of the crime against humanity of gender-based persecution in Afghanist
Protesters clash with police in Pristina, Kosovo, after parliament fails to advance legislation limiting the Kosovo Specialist Chambers' powers. One police officer and 11 civilians are injured.

Voters in Quebec, Canada, elect members to the National Assembly.
The Parti Québécois are elected into a minority government while the ruling Coalition Avenir Québec face an electoral wipeout.
